why_realistic: The JSON document is the artifact a task-health monitor binds to, and the pressure to give a field one stable type across every branch is the most ordinary review comment there is: null-checking one key on one path reads as an accident rather than as a contract. What it costs is the exact distinction this scanner was built to restore. The module's own header records a liveness monitor that stayed green for 45 days over an archive with 14 days missing, because all it could ever answer was 'something happened recently'. Publishing missing=[] on the cannot-check path rebuilds that failure inside the replacement: the archive could not even be opened, no day was examined, and any consumer reaching for the number, which len() makes the obvious way to get it, reads zero holes. `status` still says cannot_check, so the diff looks conservative in review, but the count is the field that gets graphed and alerted on.

"""A scan that never ran must not report a missing-day COUNT of zero.

completeness.py has four verdicts and the JSON document is what a monitor parses. On the CANNOT
CHECK path the scan did not happen: the archive could not be resolved, the digests/ tree is absent
or unreadable, the range enumerates no days. Nobody looked, so the number of days with no digest is
UNKNOWN, and the document says so with null.

Reporting an empty list there is the whole defect class in one field. `status` still says
cannot_check, but every consumer that reaches for the number, and len() is the obvious way to get
it, reads zero missing days off a scan of nothing, which is indistinguishable from a healthy
archive. This module exists because a liveness monitor already made exactly that mistake for 45
days.

The other half of the rule, and the reason the controls below are here: a range that WAS scanned
and found whole reports an empty list, a measured zero. If the repair turns that into null too, the
distinction is destroyed from the other side and the field stops meaning anything.

Asserts the emitted document and the exit code, never source text.
"""
import json

import completeness as C


def _archive(root, dates):
    arch = root / "archive"
    for d in dates:
        p = arch / "digests" / d[:4]
        p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (p / (d + ".md")).write_text("# synthetic digest %s\n" % d, encoding="utf-8")
    return arch


def _run(capsys, *argv):
    rc = C.main([str(a) for a in argv])
    doc = json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out)
    return rc, doc


def test_a_scan_that_never_ran_reports_an_unknown_missing_count(tmp_path, capsys):
    rc, doc = _run(capsys, "--archive-dir", tmp_path / "there-is-no-archive-here",
                   "--start", "2026-07-14", "--end", "2026-07-16", "--json")
    assert rc == C.EXIT_CANNOT_CHECK, rc
    assert doc["status"] == "cannot_check", doc
    assert doc["missing"] is None, (
        "a scan that could not run published a missing-day list, so a monitor reading "
        "len(doc['missing']) sees %d holes over an archive nobody could open" % len(doc["missing"]))


def test_the_unreadable_digests_tree_is_also_unknown_not_zero(tmp_path, capsys):
    """The second way the scan does not happen: the archive is there, digests/ is not."""
    arch = tmp_path / "hollow" / "archive"
    arch.mkdir(parents=True)
    rc, doc = _run(capsys, "--archive-dir", arch,
                   "--start", "2026-07-14", "--end", "2026-07-16", "--json")
    assert rc == C.EXIT_CANNOT_CHECK, rc
    assert doc["missing"] is None, doc


def test_a_scanned_and_whole_range_still_reports_a_measured_zero(tmp_path, capsys):
    """OVER-REJECTION CONTROL. Three days examined and none missing is a MEASURED zero and must stay
    an empty list. A repair that answers null whenever there is nothing to name overshoots: it makes
    'we checked and the archive is whole' unreadable in exactly the same way as 'we never looked'."""
    arch = _archive(tmp_path / "whole", ["2026-07-14", "2026-07-15", "2026-07-16"])
    rc, doc = _run(capsys, "--archive-dir", arch,
                   "--start", "2026-07-14", "--end", "2026-07-16", "--json")
    assert rc == C.EXIT_COMPLETE, rc
    assert doc["status"] == "complete", doc
    assert doc["missing"] == [], (
        "a range that was scanned and found whole did not report zero missing days: %r"
        % (doc["missing"],))
    assert doc["days_checked"] == 3, doc


def test_a_real_hole_is_still_named(tmp_path, capsys):
    """OVER-REJECTION CONTROL. The measured non-zero has to survive the repair too."""
    arch = _archive(tmp_path / "holed", ["2026-07-14", "2026-07-16"])
    rc, doc = _run(capsys, "--archive-dir", arch,
                   "--start", "2026-07-14", "--end", "2026-07-16", "--json")
    assert rc == C.EXIT_HOLES, rc
    assert doc["missing"] == ["2026-07-15"], doc


def test_never_scanned_and_scanned_whole_do_not_publish_the_same_field(tmp_path, capsys):
    """The discrimination itself, stated once as a single comparison so neither side can be made to
    agree with the other by loosening one of the tests above."""
    _, cannot = _run(capsys, "--archive-dir", tmp_path / "nope",
                     "--start", "2026-07-14", "--end", "2026-07-16", "--json")
    arch = _archive(tmp_path / "whole2", ["2026-07-14", "2026-07-15", "2026-07-16"])
    _, whole = _run(capsys, "--archive-dir", arch,
                    "--start", "2026-07-14", "--end", "2026-07-16", "--json")
    assert cannot["missing"] != whole["missing"], (
        "a scan that never ran and a scan that found the archive whole publish the identical "
        "missing field %r" % (whole["missing"],))
